summary: Translated the three RollTables (31 results) into `6-工作区/phase2/SYS-T1.cn.json`, shape byte-for-byte identical to the payload (tables → name / results → range key → {name?, description}). **Table names verified frozen, not trusted.** All three resolve in DO-NOT-TRANSLATE.json §`name_lookups`/table entries as T-FROZEN with call sites `actor.mjs:554` (Panic Table), `:845` (Stress Response Table), `:1067` (Panic Response Table), and glossary_alien.json maps each to itself. Emitted unchanged in English. **The Panic Table needed no new prose.** Its ten descriptions are the same source strings as `ALIENRPG.Panic1` and `Panic7–15`, which Phase 1 already delivered. I re-derived that from `lang/en.json` rather than assuming it: 1-6 and 12-12 are byte-identical to their lang English; the other eight differ only in the whitespace after `` (this table has two ASCII spaces where lang has space+U+00A0). So I reused the Phase-1 Chinese verbatim and carried this table's own whitespace, which also keeps the file at zero NBSP against an EN side of zero. **Result names are byte-equal to their lang condition value, all 19 verified mechanically** — the pairing the brief warned about holds, including TREMBLE↔`ALIENRPG.shakes` where the English differs and the Chinese must not. I checked the coupling in source: `rollPanic`/`rollStress` dispatch on the roll TOTAL, not on the result name, so a mistranslated name would not throw — it would silently render a different word beside the status-effect label in `panic-response-roll.hbs` (`name: customResults[0].name` at `actor.mjs:1246`, next to the effect toggled from the same switch). Display-only, but exactly the drift the SAME_STRING_GROUPS rule exists to stop, so the gate is worth having. The 21 Panic/Stress Response descriptions are new prose (no lang equivalent exists — the `ALIENRPG.TAH.*` keys cover only environmental conditions), written plain and instructional, second person, reusing the lock's established phrasings (濒死 / 追骰 / 余量检定 / 在恐慌结束前 / 瘫倒在地 / 茫然地凝视着虚空). 20 self-gate checks, 0 failures. Eight terms the glossary lacks are reported rather than silently coined; nine source-fidelity decisions are itemized in open_issues, several of which the controller should confirm before `fill_twin.py` propagates this to corerules and starterset.

glossary_gaps.why: The result-0 'nothing happens' row of BOTH Evolved tables. No lang key exists (`keepingcool` is in the `toRemove` list at alienrpg.mjs:267, so it is not a condition and has no ALIENRPG.* value), and no glossary row. Deliberately NOT set equal to KEEPING IT TOGETHER 保持镇定 (the classic Panic Table's row) — SAME_STRING_GROUPS does not pair them, exactly as phase1 recorded for Lose Item vs DROP ITEM. Also distinct from Keeping Guard 保持警戒. 保持冷静 collides with nothing in glossary_alien.json.

Evolved-only term, 6 occurrences across Panic Response 7-7/8-8/9-9/10-10/11-11. Not in the glossary and not in lang. An action that breaks into the turn order; 打断 is the direct rendering and does not collide with 快速动作/慢速动作.

glossary_gaps.en: turn (a character's turn in combat, 'losing your next turn')
glossary_gaps.why: HOMOGRAPH RISK — the glossary's `Turn = 节` is the middle TIME UNIT (SAME_STRING_GROUPS pairs it with Stretch for exactly that reason). 'losing your next turn' in Panic Response 7-7/8-8/9-9/10-10 is the combat turn, a different sense; rendering it 节 (5–10 minutes) would be a rules error. 出手 keeps it distinct from both 节 (Stretch) and 轮 (Round) — 回合 was rejected because Chinese TRPG usage reads it as Round.
'breaking the turn order', Panic Response 8-8 and 10-10. Falls out of the 出手 choice above; kept distinct from 先攻 (Initiative).
Panic Response 6-6, 'the #10 initiative card'. Glossary has Initiative = 先攻 but no card compound.
Panic Response 8-8, the zone descriptor that gates whether Seek Cover works. Paired with its opposite below.
Panic Response 8-8, the branch that turns Seek Cover into Scream. Glossary has Zone = 区域 but neither descriptor.

Panic Response 4-4. The rules define only Fast Action 快速动作 and Slow Action 慢速动作 — there is no third action type — so this is the author's loose synonym for Fast Action rather than a new term. Flagging because the English string is NOT 'Fast Action' and a term-drift gate may read 快速动作 here as a renamed term.

open_issues: SOURCE TYPO PRESERVED — Panic Table 7-7 ends with a stray ASCII apostrophe: `...increases by one.'`. The lang twin (ALIENRPG.Panic7) has no such character. I preserved it, so the CN ends `...各上升一级。'`. Rationale: my CN differs from the Phase-1 lock in exactly the places the table's EN differs from the lock's EN, and deleting source characters is not a translator's call. If the controller would rather the CN read clean, delete the single trailing U+0027 — nothing else changes.

NBSP DROPPED, 5 OCCURRENCES — the Panic Response Table's English carries 5 U+00A0 inside sentences (8-8 `This is an interrupt`, 10-10 `After the move`, 11-11 `Every friendly PC` and `until you or`). They are word gaps from the author's paste; Chinese has no inter-word position for them, so the CN emits 0. If a gate asserts `U+00A0 count identical to English` on pack content the way the Phase-1 lang gate did, this unit will trip it and the gate needs a mid-prose exemption — do not 'fix' it by injecting NBSPs into the Chinese.

WHITESPACE DIVERGES FROM THE LANG LOCK, DELIBERATELY — in 8 of the 10 Panic Table cells the table's own English has two ASCII spaces after `` where lang/en.json has space+U+00A0. I followed the TABLE (two ASCII spaces), not the lang value, so U+00A0 stays at 0=0 against this unit's own source. The two cells whose EN is byte-identical to lang (1-6, 12-12) reuse the lang whitespace unchanged.

EM DASH COUNT 1 -> 2 — Panic Table 9-9 English has one U+2014 (`item—the GM`); the Phase-1 lock renders it as the Chinese double dash `——`. I kept the lock. A strict per-character parity gate would see 1 vs 2. This is correct Chinese typography and matches what Phase 1 already shipped, but flagging it since I could not find a rule covering U+2014 (the register's encoding_note names only U+2013 and U+00A0).

TRAILING PERIOD DROPPED FROM ALL 21 RESULT NAMES — every English name is written as a mini-sentence (`Spooked.`, `Mess Up.`, `Keeping Cool.`). The Chinese is bare, with no `。` and no `.`, so each is byte-equal to its lang condition value per the brief's requirement and per the T-EXACT tier definition ('pure Chinese, byte-equal to a lang key... no trailing space'). A Chinese UI label does not take a sentence period. Confirm this is the house rule before fill_twin.py propagates it to two more packs.

'one Round' x3 IN PROSE (reporting per the brief's heal-time instruction) — Panic Table 10-10, 11-11 and 12-12 contain lowercase `one Round` inside sentences. These are NOT heal-time cells: there is no crit table in this pack, and `ALIENRPG.OneRound` / `OneTurn` are still deliberately English in cn.json pending the Phase-5 lockstep. The Phase-1 lock already renders this prose as 一轮 (glossary Round = 轮), so I did not deviate. No Phase-5 coupling as far as I can see, but the words are present, so it is on the record.

AMBIGUOUS GAME TERM — Panic Response 4-4: 'you need an OBSERVATION roll and a stretch of time to find the item'. Evolved renamed the middle time unit Turn -> Stretch (glossary Stretch = 节), so this could mean literally one Stretch. I read it as the English idiom (lowercase, indefinite article, no capital) and wrote 一段时间. If the controller has the Evolved text and it means the unit, change 并花上一段时间 to 并花上一节时间.

BROKEN SOURCE ENGLISH — Stress Response 7-10: 'Your action fails regardless of rolled and you gain +1 stress level.' A word is missing after 'regardless of'. Translated to the evident meaning: 无论掷出什么结果，你的动作都失败. Phrasing follows the existing lock ALIENRPG.ActionFailed = 动作失败.
MISSING FINAL PERIOD PRESERVED — Panic Table 10-10 and 14-14 have no sentence-final period in English; the Phase-1 lock also omits it, and I kept it omitted. Intentional, not an oversight.

COUPLING NOTE FOR THE CONTROLLER — I verified in source that rollPanic (actor.mjs:554), rollStress (:845) and the Panic-Response path (:1067) all dispatch on the roll TOTAL via a switch, never on the result name string, so a bad name cannot throw. The names still matter because panic-response-roll.hbs renders customResults[0].name (:1246) immediately beside the status-effect label localized from ALIENRPG.<effectid> — a mismatch would show the player two different words for one result. That is why G6/G7 are hard gates here rather than advisory.

PROPAGATION READY — no unit-local content; the file can be copied verbatim into the corerules and starterset twins by tm/fill_twin.py. Note the register lists Stress Response Table and Panic Response Table as present in all three packs but Panic Table as present in system + corerules only, so expect the starterset twin to take 2 of the 3 tables.
